- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later days.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 80+ levels), then sharply correct downward — model fails to capture this “rebound” or “mean reversion” effect.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher prices, particularly in the 70–75 range, suggesting it underweights downward momentum or overweights short-term volatility.
- Forecasts often lag true price movements by 1–3 days, especially in the 60–70 range — model is slow to react to downward trends.
- Model fails to capture the “drop-off” after peak prices (e.g., 80+), underestimating the rate of decline and missing the “tail” of the price correction.
- Model overreacts to recent high prices, producing overly optimistic forecasts when prices are already trending down — especially in the 70–75 range.
- Model underestimates the “mean reversion” effect — fails to recognize that prices often return to a lower range after a spike, especially after 75–80.
- Model tends to smooth out volatility, underestimating sharp downward corrections and overestimating gradual declines.
- Model is overly confident in short-term momentum, especially in the 70–75 range, leading to overestimation of upward continuation.
- Model underestimates the “reversal” effect after a spike — fails to recognize that prices often drop sharply after a peak, especially in the 75–80 range.
